text: This is version 1 of the Service Contract Catalog and it inherits no section, ID, number or date.
why: No earlier version of the family exists.
impact: None on content; the change log starts here.

text: The Ownership Map Endpoints sheet is read as the operation set per owning service; the per-service base path comes from Architecture v5 slide 41 and Template and Rules §R4, and the final path and payload belong to API Specification v5.
why: Two sources describe the REST surface at different levels.
read: Ownership Map v1, Endpoints sheet; Architecture v5 slide 41; Template and Rules §R4
impact: No operation is added or removed; only the base path is applied.

text: The activity contract jars are named by their task queue and Java package root; the coordinates are left open for allocation.
why: The coordinates are not stated in any source.
read: Architecture v5 slide 11; Temporal and Drools Design slide 12
impact: The build story allocates coordinates; no contract changes.

text: ApprovalDecided and ReportPublished are recorded with the placeholder for their consumers rather than an assumed consumer.
why: The event catalogue names no consumer.

text: This catalogue states the AsyncAPI artefact, CloudEvents 1.0 binary mode and BACKWARD compatibility, and does not name a registry product.
why: The product is not specified in the read set.
impact: The platform work chooses the product; the contract rule holds either way.

text: The rule that route services reach shared capabilities through Temporal is read as covering decision, document, payment, partner and communications, the five capabilities the slide note names; the rwb-source-data reference reads stay REST, one hop and cached.
why: The matrix gives both REST cells to rwb-source-data and the rule.
read: Architecture v5 slide 13 and its notes
impact: Three REST pairs stay synchronous; no route service gains a REST call to a shared capability.

text: The Enterprise AI call is carried as an edge contract with a recorded-response double; no payload is stated.
why: The integration contract is not specified.
impact: P10 tests against the double until the endpoint contract is agreed.

text: The S5 to P6 Temporal cell is kept with the placeholder and no interface is invented.
why: The matrix and the service contract disagree.
impact: One Temporal row stays open in the S5 contract.

text: Every cross-service pair is class C for the consuming story and class I for the integration story of the later wave; every pair that touches gateway-bff, ACE Common, the ACE database, Enterprise AI, the bank file channels or partners is class X.
why: Template and Rules §R5.4 defines the classes but not the assignment per pair.
impact: No consumer story waits for a provider build.

text: No release date is held in this catalogue; the dates in the Release Plan are unchanged and every one is tentative.
why: Decision U7 and DL48 fix this, and the source has no release date.
read: Template and Rules §R1 (U7); Architecture v5 slide 38
impact: None; this catalogue carries no date but the document date.
